item.title: Round money with round_money, not bare division
item.content: Always wrap monetary results in ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never return a bare Decimal division or use Python's round()/quantize(), which use banker's rounding.

review_comments: [team convention] Round money only with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent). Python's round() and a bare Decimal.quantize() use banker's rounding and give wrong invoice totals.

item.title: Use BillingError with machine-readable codes
item.content: Raise `BillingError(code, detail)` from `ledgerly/errors.py` for domain validation failures, using existing codes like "invalid_state" and "negative_amount" rather than ValueError.

item.title: Money-moving ops need idempotency_key
item.content: Every operation that moves money or changes a payment/credit must accept a keyword-only `idempotency_key`; check `ledgerly.audit.events()` for an existing entry with that key and return early without reapplying, and include `idempotency_key` in the audit entry written.

review_comments: [team convention] Every operation that moves money or changes a payment/credit must accept a keyword-only `idempotency_key`. If an audit entry with the same key already exists (ledgerly.audit.events()), return without applying the operation again, and include `idempotency_key` in the audit entry you write. Introduced after the double-refund incident INC-204.

[team convention] Support-initiated refunds and credits above 500.00 need a second approver (finance policy FIN-2026-03): accept a keyword-only `approved_by` and raise BillingError("approval_required") when it is missing for amounts above the threshold.
